---
title: "Energy Demand: electricity"
subtitle: "Monthly electricity demand in the United States and five Southeast Asian economies, on one definition from one source"
---

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import Markdown
from itables import init_notebook_mode, show

from pdi import site

init_notebook_mode(connected=False)

latest, meta = site.load("energy", "demand_latest")
history, history_meta = site.load("energy", "demand_history")
finding = meta.get("finding")
```

Electricity demand is one of the few activity measures published monthly, in the same unit,
for both regions. This page shows how fast demand is growing in each economy and whether the
latest month was out of the ordinary. It does not explain the moves: weather, industry and
new data centres all change demand, and nothing here separates them.

## Latest month

```{python}
#| output: asis
if latest.empty:
    print(site.empty_state(meta, "Electricity demand"))
else:
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
    for _, r in latest.assign(latest_month=pd.to_datetime(latest["latest_month"])).iterrows():
        print(f'- {site.finding_badge(finding)} {r["sentence"]}')
    flagged = int(latest["flagged"].sum())
    print(f'\n{flagged} of {len(latest)} economies had an unusual latest month (a monthly move '
          f'{meta["flag_z"]} spreads or more from what that calendar month usually brings, the '
          f'[same rule as the Macro Monitor](../methodology.qmd#energy-demand)). '
          f'The economies report with different delays, so the latest months differ.')
    if meta.get("not_covered"):
        print(f'\nNot covered: {", ".join(meta["not_covered"])} (no monthly demand at the source).')
```

```{python}
if not latest.empty:
    t = latest.assign(
        latest_month=pd.to_datetime(latest["latest_month"]).dt.strftime("%Y-%m"),
        first_month=pd.to_datetime(latest["first_month"]).dt.strftime("%Y-%m"),
        Flag=latest["flagged"].map({True: "Unusual", False: ""}),
    )[["name", "latest_month", "demand_twh", "gwh_per_day", "yoy_pct", "year_yoy_pct", "z",
       "Flag", "first_month"]].rename(columns={
        "name": "Economy", "latest_month": "Latest month", "demand_twh": "Demand, TWh",
        "gwh_per_day": "GWh per day", "yoy_pct": "Month on a year earlier, %",
        "year_yoy_pct": "Last 12 months on the 12 before, %", "z": "Spreads",
        "first_month": "History starts"}).round(
        {"Demand, TWh": 1, "GWh per day": 0, "Month on a year earlier, %": 1,
         "Last 12 months on the 12 before, %": 1, "Spreads": 1})
    show(t, paging=False, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
```

## Demand since the base year

Each line is demand per day as an index, so that an economy using 5 TWh a month and one using
400 fit on one chart. The lines are a 12-month average, which removes the seasons.

```{python}
if history.empty:
    display(Markdown(site.empty_state(history_meta, "Demand history")))
else:
    h = history.assign(period=pd.to_datetime(history["period"])).sort_values("period")
    h["smooth"] = h.groupby("country")["index"].transform(
        lambda s: s.rolling(12, min_periods=12).mean())
    h = h[h["period"].dt.year >= meta["index_base_year"]].dropna(subset=["smooth"])
    fig = px.line(h, x="period", y="smooth", color="name",
                  labels={"smooth": f'Index, {meta["index_base_year"]} = 100', "period": "",
                          "name": ""})
    fig.update_layout(height=420, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10))
    fig.show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not history.empty:
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
```

## Change on a year earlier, month by month

```{python}
if not history.empty:
    h = history.assign(period=pd.to_datetime(history["period"])).dropna(subset=["yoy_pct"])
    h = h[h["period"] >= h["period"].max() - pd.DateOffset(months=36)]
    fig = px.line(h, x="period", y="yoy_pct", color="name",
                  labels={"yoy_pct": "Demand per day on a year earlier, %", "period": "",
                          "name": ""})
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_width=1, line_color="gray")
    fig.update_layout(height=380, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10))
    fig.show()
```

    print(site.finding_line(finding))
